Question B-003-020-010.

Why the correct answer is right: Turning off the transmitter and disconnecting the transmission line removes radio frequency (RF) energy from the antenna system before repairs begin.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Be sure the antenna structure is properly grounded": Grounding may be part of lightning or static safety, but it does not prove the transmitter cannot feed RF into the antenna during repair.
- sourceIndex 2: "Plan the operation in the shortest possible time to minimize fatigue": Good planning matters, yet shorter work time does not remove the electrical/RF hazard from an energized feed line.
- sourceIndex 3: "Ensure all masts to be installed are sufficiently light": Mast weight affects handling, but the named precaution before antenna repair is to de-energize and disconnect the RF source.
